agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby council to vote on updated Amenity Cost Charges program
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is set to vote on an updated Amenity Cost Charges (ACC) program and related bylaw amendments. If approved, this would change the fees developers pay to help fund community amenities like parks, community centres, and libraries when new development happens. The proposed bylaw would set new charge rates and rules for collecting these fees. This is not yet approved — council will consider the proposal at an upcoming meeting.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision date — if approved, these charges will affect development costs for new construction projects in Burnaby.
agenda_briefs.source_body:
7.1 ACC PROGRAM & BYLAW AMENDMENT
Purpose: To request Council approval of an amended Amenity Cost Charges (ACC) Program & related amendments to the Burnaby Amenity Cost Charges Bylaw.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby Council to urge Province to restore climate action funding
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider sending a letter to the provincial government asking them to renew funding for the Local Government Climate Action Program (LGCAP). This program helps local governments pay for projects that reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The Province recently cut this funding, and Burnaby is asking them to bring it back. This is a proposed advocacy action — no new rules or fees for businesses are being voted on yet.
agenda_briefs.action_required: No action needed from you right now. Watch for the Council decision — if approved, the letter will be sent to the Province.
agenda_briefs.source_body:
7.2 ADVOCACY FOR RENEWED PROVINCIAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT CLIMATE ACTION PROGRAM FUNDING
Purpose: To provide Council with an update on the provincial Local Government Climate Action Program (LGCAP) funding cut and request Mayor and Council forward a letter to the Province to advocate for renewed funding for LGCAP.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby to vote on rental replacement rule changes
agenda_briefs.summary: Council will consider minor amendments to Stream 1 of the Rental Use Zoning Policy. These changes would align the policy with recent updates to rental replacement requirements. If approved, the amendments could affect how developers and landlords handle replacing rental units when redeveloping property in Burnaby. The proposal is on the agenda for an upcoming council meeting and has not yet been enacted.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision — these changes could affect your rental replacement obligations.
agenda_briefs.source_body:
7.3 PROPOSED AMENDMENTS TO RENTAL USE ZONING POLICY STREAM 1 - RENTAL REPLACEMENT
Purpose: To propose minor amendments to Stream 1 of the Rental Use Zoning Policy to align with recent changes to rental replacement requirements.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Burnaby Council to comment on Metro Vancouver growth strategy amendment
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council is considering a comment letter opposing Metro Vancouver Amendment Bylaw No. 1456, 2026, which would eliminate the prohibition on new Special Study Areas (SSAs) and allow any member jurisdiction to request new SSAs of any size and location before December 31, 2027. SSAs make it easier to re-designate Agricultural, Rural, Conservation and Recreation, and Employment lands and to expand the Urban Containment Boundary, facilitating sprawl with added costs to regional DCCs and TransLink services, environmental harm, loss of food-producing land, speculative pressure, and traffic congestion. The bylaw also adds a 152-hectare SSA in Langley Township on Fraser Highway to re-designate Rural lands to Industrial.
agenda_briefs.action_required: Watch for the council decision on this comment letter — it could signal future changes to regional growth rules that affect your business.

agenda_briefs.title: Proposed: Council to vote on funding for Kensington Overpass and tunnel murals
agenda_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council will consider a proposal to approve funding for new artistic murals on the Kensington Overpass pillars and the Lougheed Pedestrian Tunnel South entrance walls. minutes_briefs.title: Council approved amended Amenity Cost Charges program and bylaw
minutes_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council unanimously approved amendments to the Amenity Cost Charges (ACC) program and Bylaw 2024. ACCs are fees developers pay to the city to help fund community amenities like parks, community centres, and libraries that are needed because of new development. The approved changes update how these charges are calculated and applied. Council also approved a communication plan and authorized staff to begin consulting with the public and stakeholders about the changes. The City Solicitor has been directed to prepare the formal bylaw amendments, which will be brought back to Council for final adoption.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you are a developer or property owner planning a project in Burnaby, review the amended ACC program details to understand how the new charges will affect your development costs.
minutes_briefs.source_body: THAT the proposed amended Amenity Cost Charge program set out in Attachment 1, as outlined in the report titled “ACC Program & Bylaw Amendment”, dated July 14, 2026, be approved; THAT the communication plan outlined in Section 4.0 of the report be approved and that staff be authorized to commence consultation; and THAT the City Solicitor be authorized to bring forward amendments to Burnaby Amenity Cost Charges Bylaw 2024, substantially as set out in Attachment 2. CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY

minutes_briefs.title: Council refers Sidley Street rezoning back to staff for taller building review
minutes_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council voted unanimously to send the rezoning application for 5168, 5189, and 5192 Sidley Street back to city staff. The original plan was for a six-storey market rental building under the Royal Oak Community Plan. Council wants staff to come back with information on the best value proposal for the land, including looking at a revised design for a much taller 12 to 20-storey building. This means the project is not approved yet and will be reworked before coming back to Council for a final decision.
minutes_briefs.action_required: No immediate action needed; monitor future Council meetings for the revised staff report on the Sidley Street rezoning.

CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY

minutes_briefs.title: Council approved first readings of Burnaby Amenity Cost Charges Bylaw No. 14837
minutes_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council voted unanimously to give first, second, and third readings to Bylaw No. 14837, which amends the Amenity Cost Charges Bylaw. This is an early step in the bylaw process — the amendment is not yet final. Council will need to hold a public hearing and adopt the bylaw at a later meeting before it takes effect. The amendment likely changes how the city collects fees from developers to pay for community amenities like parks, community centres, and libraries.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you are a developer or property owner, monitor future council agendas for the public hearing and final adoption of Bylaw No. 14837.
minutes_briefs.source_body: THAT Bylaw No. 14837 be now reada first, second and third time. CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY

minutes_briefs.title: Council approved first readings of Housing Agreement Bylaw for 6887 Palm Avenue
minutes_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council voted unanimously to give first, second, and third readings to Bylaw No. 14841, which establishes a housing agreement for the property at 6887 Palm Avenue. This bylaw will secure the land for affordable housing purposes, meaning the owner must keep the units affordable as specified in the agreement. The decision is a step toward final adoption, but the bylaw is not yet in full effect.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you own or manage property at 6887 Palm Avenue, review the housing agreement terms to ensure compliance with affordability requirements.
minutes_briefs.source_body: THAT Bylaw No. 14841 be now reada first, second and third time. CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY

minutes_briefs.title: Council adopts bylaw repealing housing agreement at 5227 Lane Street
minutes_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council voted unanimously to adopt Bylaw No. 14836, which repeals a housing agreement tied to the property at 5227 Lane Street. A housing agreement is a legal deal between the city and a property owner that sets rules about how the property can be used, often to keep it affordable. Repealing this agreement removes those restrictions, which could change what can be built or done on the site. The decision is final and the bylaw is now in effect.
minutes_briefs.action_required: If you own or manage property at 5227 Lane Street, review the repealed housing agreement to understand what new uses or developments are now allowed.
minutes_briefs.source_body: THAT Bylaw No. 14836 be now reada final time and adopted. CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY

minutes_briefs.summary: Burnaby Council voted unanimously to have the Mayor write a letter to the Provincial Transportation and Transit Minister.
